```suggestion
	if (multimesh->indirect) { // Necessitates altering the command buffer to account for the new vertex count, going to assume at this time one surface.
```

You shouldn't be adding all surfaces together. Each surface results in one draw call, so each surface needs its own entry in the command buffer. Then, when drawing, you use the `p_offset` argument to offset into the command buffer based on what surface you are drawing.
Please remove these extra curly brackets. They add too much indentation here

I am unsure what you mean, would that mean that I technically need multiple command buffers for each surface? Each command buffer has to contain the vertex/index count of the mesh it's rendering, and if it is the command buffer for one surface, and it is supposed to be used to render another, it cannot be the same buffer unless I'm updating the vertex count on the command buffer with each draw call for each surface.

I am quite sure I am incorrect in what I am thinking here.

It should be one command buffer, but that one command buffer will hold the data for multiple surfaces. Instead of holding one instance of the command struct, it will hold multiple. 

Then, when you draw, you just pass an offset into the command to tell the GPU which instance to use.
